record.paper_title: Open Problems on Open Algebraic Varieties (Montreal 1994 Problems)
record.original_question: Rigidity conjecture: Is every smooth Q-acyclic surface of log-general type rigid?

evidence.quote: 1.3. RIGIDITY CONJECTURE (H. Flenner-M. Zaidenberg [FlZa]). Any smooth Q-acyclic surface X of log-general type is rigid.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a smooth complex algebraic surface that is $\mathbb{Q}$-acyclic, meaning $H_i(X;\mathbb{Q}) = 0$ for all $i > 0$. Fix a smooth projective compactification $\overline{X}$ of $X$ such that the boundary $D = \overline{X}\setminus X$ is a simple normal crossing divisor, and let $K_{\overline{X}}$ denote the canonical divisor of $\overline{X}$. Say that $X$ is of log-general type if the logarithmic Kodaira dimension $\overline{\kappa}(X) := \kappa(\overline{X}, K_{\overline{X}}+D)$ equals $2$. Say that the pair $(\overline{X}, D)$ is rigid if it admits no non-trivial equisingular logarithmic deformations, i.e. $H^1(\overline{X}, T_{\overline{X}}(-\log D)) = 0$, where $T_{\overline{X}}(-\log D)$ is the logarithmic tangent sheaf.

Prove or disprove: every smooth $\mathbb{Q}$-acyclic surface $X$ of log-general type is rigid in the sense above.
artifact.status_search_result: The Flenner–Zaidenberg rigidity conjecture for smooth Q-acyclic (Q-homology plane) surfaces of log-general type continues to be cited as an open problem in subsequent literature on Q-homology planes and rational cuspidal curves (e.g., work of Palka and others). No verifiable proof or counterexample in the smooth case was located via web search; the status appears unresolved in general.

status_evidence.title: Classification of planar rational cuspidal curves I
status_evidence.snippet: References to the Flenner–Zaidenberg weak rigidity conjecture and related conjectures appear as still-open guiding problems.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is referenced as an open guiding problem in later research on related topics.

status_evidence.title: Classification of singular Q-homology planes I
status_evidence.snippet: Work of Palka on Q-homology planes addresses structure but does not resolve the smooth log-general type rigidity conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work on Q-homology planes does not announce a resolution of the smooth-case rigidity conjecture.
